title: Abraham Wald's WWII Bullet-Hole Map: Stop Copying Lucky Outliers
alt_title_1: The 1943 Bomber Armor Insight That Saves Investors From Ruin
alt_title_2: Survivorship Bias Explained: Why Missing Failures Matter Most
description_hook: In 1943, mathematician Abraham Wald at Columbia's Statistical Research Group stopped military planners from armoring the bullet-riddled wings of returning bombers, pointing to the missing planes hit in the engines instead. Here is how Survivorship Bias distorts wealth advice.

scenes.headline: The 1943 Bullet-Hole Mistake Nearly Everyone Makes
scenes.stat_label: WWII BOMBER ARMOR PUZZLE AT COLUMBIA
bullets: Returning planes had wings covered in shrapnel holes
Officers wanted extra armor placed right over the holes
scenes.narration: In 1943, military officers inspected bullet-riddled World War Two bombers and nearly armored the exact wrong parts of the plane until a mathematician intervened.
scenes.source: Abraham Wald, Statistical Research Group at Columbia University (1943)

scenes.headline: Abraham Wald Counted the Planes That Never Returned
bullets: Planes hit in the wings survived the flight home
Planes hit in the engines crashed before reaching the hangar
scenes.narration: Working at Columbia University's Statistical Research Group, mathematician Abraham Wald noticed returning wings were covered in holes while engines were clean. He advised armoring the spotless engines: planes hit there never returned.
scenes.source: Abraham Wald, 'A Method of Estimating Plane Vulnerability', SRG Memo (1943)

scenes.headline: Copying Visible Winners While Ignoring Silent Graveyards
scenes.left_body: Copies 1 lucky 50x gamble -> ignores 999 silent wipeouts
scenes.right_body: Studies failure modes first -> compounds high-probability bets
scenes.narration: Financial media commits that exact Survivorship Bias daily, interviewing reckless leverage gamblers or college-dropout billionaires while ignoring thousands of identical bets that went bankrupt.

scenes.headline: Always Inspect the Missing Denominator
scenes.stat_label: SURVIVAL FIRST -> DECADES OF UNBROKEN COMPOUNDING
scenes.stat_subtext: Avoid catastrophic downside before chasing upside
scenes.narration: Before copying any viral wealth or business playbook, inspect the denominator: look at where the missing casualties failed, and optimize for repeatable base rates.

scenes.headline: Armor Your Financial Engines First
bullets: Never risk survival margin on low-probability bets
Build durable skills and cash reserves that prevent ruin
scenes.narration: Armor your engines against ruin first, because compounding only rewards builders who stay in the air.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin risk rule inspired by Abraham Wald (1943)
